question: What anatomical barrier significantly limits systemic drug penetration into the anterior segment of the eye?

options.A: The lens capsule and vitreous humor

explanation: The cornea and blood-aqueous barrier protect intraocular structures and restrict the entry of systemically administered drugs, making topical administration necessary for anterior segment conditions. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h1)

question: Why must otic drops containing aminoglycosides be avoided when the tympanic membrane is ruptured?

options.A: They can enter the middle ear and cause permanent sensorineural hearing loss
options.B: They will immediately crystallize and block the external auditory canal
options.C: They neutralize normal flora and worsen bacterial resistance instantly
options.D: They cause severe systemic hypertension through rapid mucosal absorption

explanation: A compromised tympanic membrane allows otic drops to cross into the middle and inner ear, where ototoxic drugs can damage cochlear hair cells and lead to permanent deafness. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h1)

question: Which class of glaucoma medication primarily increases uveoscleral outflow of aqueous humor?
explanation: Prostaglandin analogues like latanoprost reduce intraocular pressure by enhancing the uveoscleral outflow pathway and are dosed once daily. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h2)

question: A patient with a history of bronchial asthma is prescribed timolol eye drops for glaucoma. What is the most significant clinical concern with this prescription?

options.A: Topical timolol inactivates inhaled asthma medications instantly
options.B: It will cause irreversible widening of the pupil diameter
options.C: The drug will completely stop aqueous humor production permanently
options.D: Systemic absorption can trigger severe bronchospasm

explanation: Even though administered topically, beta-blockers like timolol can enter the systemic circulation and provoke bronchoconstriction in patients with reactive airway diseases. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h2)

question: What is the primary pharmacological effect of a cycloplegic eye drop?

options.A: Contraction of the pupillary sphincter muscle and miosis
options.B: Suppression of bacterial growth in the conjunctival sac
options.C: Paralysis of the ciliary muscle and loss of accommodation
options.D: Increased systemic blood pressure via alpha-receptor agonism

explanation: Cycloplegics block acetylcholine at muscarinic receptors on the ciliary body, paralyzing the focusing mechanism and causing mydriasis. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h3)

question: Why are short-acting cycloplegics preferred over long-acting agents like atropine for routine diagnostic refraction in adults?

options.A: They do not cause any degree of papillary dilation
options.B: They lower intraocular pressure much faster than atropine
options.C: They completely eliminate the risk of systemic absorption
options.D: They prevent prolonged blurring of vision and photophobia

explanation: Long-acting agents like atropine can blur near vision and cause light sensitivity for over a week, whereas agents like tropicamide wear off in hours. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h3)

question: Which of the following is a recognized long-term complication of prolonged topical corticosteroid eye drop use?

options.A: Spontaneous rupture of the corneal stroma
options.B: Permanent miosis and atrophy of the iris sphincter
options.C: Total destruction of the lacrimal gland and dry eyes
options.D: Development of cataracts and elevated intraocular pressure

explanation: Extended use of ophthalmic steroids can induce secondary glaucoma and posterior subcapsular cataracts, requiring careful clinical monitoring. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h4)

question: A patient is prescribed both an antibiotic eye drop and a corticosteroid drop for a post-surgical eye. What is the standard instruction regarding administration intervals?

options.A: Mix both medications in the bottle to save application time
options.B: Apply them simultaneously using a single drop combination
options.C: Instill the steroid first so it opens the tissue for the antibiotic
options.D: Wait at least five minutes between drops to prevent washout

explanation: Staggering topical ophthalmic medications by at least five minutes ensures the first drop is fully absorbed and not washed out or diluted by the second drop. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h4)

question: What is the primary clinical purpose of applying fluorescein sodium dye to the eye?

options.A: To provide long-lasting local anesthesia during tonometry
options.B: To measure baseline tear production in dry eye syndrome
options.C: To visualize corneal abrasions and epithelial defects under cobalt blue light
options.D: To permanently stain foreign bodies for easy surgical excision

explanation: Fluorescein pools in areas where the corneal epithelium is damaged, glowing brilliantly under cobalt blue light to reveal scratches or ulcers. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h5)

question: Why is it strictly prohibited to dispense topical ocular anesthetics for a patient to take home for pain relief?

options.A: It permanently dilates the pupil and prevents light accommodation
options.B: It can cause severe corneal damage, masking injury and leading to ulceration
options.C: It completely stops tear production, causing instant blindness
options.D: It triggers immediate systemic allergic shock within minutes

explanation: Repeated use of topical anesthetics damages the corneal epithelium and inhibits healing, predisposing the eye to severe infections and neurotrophic keratitis. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h5)

question: What is the primary function of cerumenolytic otic drops?

options.A: To destroy fungal spores lining the external auditory canal
options.B: To paralyze middle ear ossicles during surgical procedures
options.C: To soften and break down impacted earwax for easier removal
options.D: To lower intracranial pressure transmitted through the inner ear

explanation: Cerumenolytics soften hardened cerumen, facilitating gentle ear irrigation or manual extraction without damaging the canal. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h6)

question: Why are systemic antibiotics preferred over ear drops for treating uncomplicated acute otitis media?

options.A: Ear drops cause immediate rupture of the tympanic membrane
options.B: Systemic drugs bypass the liver and concentrate only in the mastoid air cells
options.C: Oral antibiotics are cheaper and have fewer gastrointestinal side effects
options.D: Topical drops cannot cross an intact tympanic membrane to reach the middle ear

explanation: Because the tympanic membrane acts as a barrier, drops placed in the external canal cannot reach infections in the middle ear cavity unless a perforation exists. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h6)

question: How should the nurse position the pinna when administering ear drops to an adult patient?
explanation: Pulling the adult pinna upward and backward straightens the S-shaped external auditory canal, allowing medication to flow down to the tympanic membrane. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h7)

question: What is the clinical purpose of performing nasolacrimal occlusion (pressing the inner corner of the eye) immediately after instilling an eye drop?

options.A: To seal any micro-perforations present in the lower eyelid
options.B: To reduce systemic absorption of the drug through the mucous membranes
options.C: To spread the medication evenly across the entire cornea instantly
options.D: To stimulate lacrimal gland secretion and wash away debris

explanation: Punctal occlusion blocks the drop from entering the tear duct and nasal passages, minimizing systemic side effects from potent drugs like timolol. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h7)

question: What critical instruction should be given to a patient prescribed eye drops that cause mydriasis and cycloplegia?

options.A: Store the open bottle in a kitchen freezer to preserve potency
options.B: Discontinue the drug as soon as mild blurring of vision occurs
options.C: Rinse the eye with sterile water immediately after application
options.D: Avoid driving or operating machinery until vision clears

explanation: Mydriatics and cycloplegics paralyze accommodation and dilate the pupil, causing blurred vision and photophobia that make hazardous activities unsafe. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h8)

question: Why is adherence counseling particularly critical for patients newly diagnosed with chronic open-angle glaucoma in Nigeria?

options.A: Glaucoma medications lose all chemical stability if a single dose is skipped
options.B: Missed doses immediately trigger severe eye pain and acute vomiting
options.C: Patients can easily synthesize alternative herbal drops if commercial drugs run out
options.D: The disease is painless and stealthy, and untreated pressure causes silent, irreversible blindness

explanation: Because chronic glaucoma progresses without early pain or warning signs, patients often stop medication if they feel fine, risking permanent optic nerve damage. [learn more](GNS215_U6_T4#GNS215_U6_T4_h8)
